reviews.title: What a nightmare and I’ve only been a…
reviews.content: What a nightmare and I’ve only been a business customer for 2 days! I should have known this wasn’t going to go well when I realized my Account Rep, who is trying to sign me up and sell me services for my business, didn’t have a direct phone or email address and could only call me after initiate a request. Keep in mind this is the most important and involved interaction I’ll probably ever have with Verizon and the time they should be most eager to talk to me but no, even now I am kept at arms length and denied the ability to call my sales rep to work on my corporate transfer. I can just imagine what trying to speak to someone will be like when the contracts are all signed. On top of this, the transfer has been a total fail. So many problems, devices that are unusable due to problems with porting, compatibility and shipping. Total frustration but I can’t speak to anyone. No less than a dozen times I’ve tried to call for help only to get trapped in their Orwellian phone directly and an answering AI who lives to simply hang up on you when you can’t answer a question you couldn’t possibly know. The best you can hope for is being directed to a another customer service number which will waste just as much of your time. You cannot bypass the system. You cannot beg the AI for human assistance or push any button to direct to live help. Even the website chat windows takes a science degree to navigate to place that will allow a human to assist you. Once you get in the queue they hit you with the “volume is high” excuse like they’ve never answered a chat before and you are forced to wait 30+ minutes for help. Good look once you get it because verifying yourself will make you wish you’d just accepted your fate and choose to string two cans together instead. Hate this company and their complete lack of service.

reviews.title: Loyal Customer Ignored After 8 Hours of Calls and No Resolution
reviews.content: I’veI’ve been a loyal Verizon customer for many years, but this recent experience left me feeling completely unvalued. On November 1, 2025, I canceled my Disney, Hulu, and ESPN bundle through the Verizon app because I wanted to open a Hulu + Live TV account. Verizon doesn’t allow that upgrade within the bundle, so I removed it. The app said I’d still have access until November 8, but that continued access kept my Hulu account linked to Verizon’s billing. Because of this, I couldn’t sign up for Hulu Live until Verizon released the account on the 8th.Between November 1 and 5, I spent over eight hours in chats and phone calls repeating the same issue. I was told to call Hulu, then told only Verizon could fix it. My case was closed without resolution, and I never received the promised callback.This should have been a simple fix, yet it turned into days of frustration. I’ve always paid on time and stayed loyal, but this experience made me feel my time and loyalty mean nothing to Verizon. I truly hope Verizon takes accountability and improves how it supports long-time customers.

reviews.title: Title: Horrible Service and Unfair Billing Practices
reviews.content: I’ve been a Verizon customer for over 5 years and I’ve never experienced such terrible service. I have a business account, and after I moved to a new location about six months ago, I didn’t even use my Verizon internet once — simply because I hadn’t set up service at my new address yet.About five months ago, I called Verizon to close my account, but their representative convinced me to keep paying for my phone line, saying it would be easier since my equipment was already paid off. I trusted them. That was a huge mistake.Now, after six months of paying for a service I never used, I decided to finally close everything. But when I called, instead of helping me, Verizon forced me to pay for another month — even though I clearly explained that I haven’t been using the service at all.Their customer service is unbelievably slow and unhelpful, their website and mobile app constantly malfunction, and their billing practices are beyond unfair. Verizon only cares about money, not their customers. I’m done with them, and I’ll make sure everyone I know hears about this experience.Stay far away from Verizon — especially if you value honesty and fair treatment

reviews.title: I'll bet Verizon's million-dollar…
reviews.content: I'll bet Verizon's million-dollar executives are scratching their heads over their Champagne-and-caviar lunches, wondering why T-Mobile is eating their lunch and stealing their customers. I'll also bet that is why they have had to lease data space to Cox Communications for their new Cox Mobile service at significant savings over their own pricing. This kind of business strategy is thoughtless at best, and suicidal at worst. Cox's entry and use of Verizon's towers will only hasten Verizon's demise as the premier carrier in the United States. In fact, Cox goes so far as to stop "just short" of advertising that it uses Verizon towers. And when you talk with Cox Mobile salespeople, all they speak about is that they're running on Verizon's network. I wonder, and scratch my head, walking into the local corporate Verizon store and see two, maybe three customers milling about, waiting for four, yes, four, Verizon salespeople who are laughing and talking amongst themselves, why Verizon now finds itself in the position it is in.I waited over ten minutes last night at the Verizon store after leaving the T-Mobile store across the street. T-Mobile had five or six working staffers trying to keep up with twice as many customers. And Verizon continues to wonder — and is only now trying to catch up — with all sorts of incentives for new and existing customers. And by the way, those "incentives" come with all kinds of contractual agreements, including three years of indentured servitude to Verizon.While T-Mobile has its share of problems — it has oversold its services, has inadequately trained Filipino agents, and hour-plus-long phone and in-store wait times — Cox Mobile also has significant issues, having tried to enter the realm of Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T on two prior occasions and failed abysmally each time. And Cox also has incompetent offshore contracted agents, just as T-Mobile, Verizon, and AT&T do. And let's not forget AT&T, with ridiculously high prices, poor offshore customer service, and faltering service. Does anyone wonder whether Verizon will be the ultimate loser in this scenario, just as Sears, Pan Am, Kmart, and TWA, and a host of others, who thought they were too large and important to fail?If I were Verizon, I'd start brown-bagging it instead of caviar and Champagne, and look within, instead of what they've been doing for years. The market is changing, and Verizon needs to adapt. It's time to compete with intelligence, not just size and reputation.

reviews.title: I started service with Verizon from…
reviews.content: I started service with Verizon from August 2, 2025, and disconnected on September 8, 2025. Here's what happened:I was charged twice on my first bill. The first charge was labeled as "First Billing," and the second charge covered the period from August 3 to September 2, 2025 — even though this was all within my first month of service.After I disconnected my line on September 8, Verizon kept my account open until October 4, 2025, and charged me for that extra time without my consent. When I contacted customer service, they blamed it on "company policy" and refused to issue a refund.In summary: I used Verizon's service for 1 month and 6 days, but I was charged for 2 months and 6 days.DON'T DO BUSINESS WITH VERIZON! BIG SCAMMER!

reviews.title: We’ve been with Verizon for 30+ years
reviews.content: We’ve been with Verizon for 30+ years! And now we’ve been lied to enough!!! Spoke with a representative early August, was told we were eligible for new phones at no cost, (we had to send old phones in) no problem!! LIES LIES apparently! Spent part of the month of August and all of September speaking with various representatives, and receiving various explanations!!! Seems each had their own agenda!!  Got frustrated and emailed Excutive services. Thought that maybe someone might actually do their job! WRONG! I gave her dates, times, and names of individuals that I had spoken with! She assured me she would get the answers! LIES!!!! She called me a month later and says that the charges are accurate?? I asked her if she had listened to the call from August 2nd in reference to the phones being free? She replied that she had NOT! I asked her to review the conversation with myself on the phone! She informed me that that wasn’t possible! I asked her if she had listened to the call, she stated that no she had NOT. I asked her to do that, she stated that she could not listen to the call because it was now too late as they only keep the recording for 30 days?? Now Verizon wants to charge me exonerated fees and equipment charges! I try to remain loyal as I’m a small business owner myself. Guess it’s time to move to a new carrier (T-Mobile is eager for my business)

reviews.title: What a nightmare and I’ve only been a…
reviews.content: What a nightmare and I’ve only been a business customer for 2 days! I should have known this wasn’t going to go well when I realized my Account Rep, who is trying to sign me up and sell me services for my business, didn’t have a direct phone or email address and could only call me after initiate a request. Keep in mind this is the most important and involved interaction I’ll probably ever have with Verizon and the time they should be most eager to talk to me but no, even now I am kept at arms length and denied the ability to call my sales rep to work on my corporate transfer. I can just imagine what trying to speak to someone will be like when the contracts are all signed. On top of this, the transfer has been a total fail. So many problems, devices that are unusable due to problems with porting, compatibility and shipping. Total frustration but I can’t speak to anyone. No less than a dozen times I’ve tried to call for help only to get trapped in their Orwellian phone directly and an answering AI who lives to simply hang up on you when you can’t answer a question you couldn’t possibly know. The best you can hope for is being directed to a another customer service number which will waste just as much of your time. You cannot bypass the system. You cannot beg the AI for human assistance or push any button to direct to live help. Even the website chat windows takes a science degree to navigate to place that will allow a human to assist you. Once you get in the queue they hit you with the “volume is high” excuse like they’ve never answered a chat before and you are forced to wait 30+ minutes for help. Good look once you get it because verifying yourself will make you wish you’d just accepted your fate and choose to string two cans together instead. Hate this company and their complete lack of service.

reviews.title: Loyal Customer Ignored After 8 Hours of Calls and No Resolution
reviews.content: I’veI’ve been a loyal Verizon customer for many years, but this recent experience left me feeling completely unvalued. On November 1, 2025, I canceled my Disney, Hulu, and ESPN bundle through the Verizon app because I wanted to open a Hulu + Live TV account. Verizon doesn’t allow that upgrade within the bundle, so I removed it. The app said I’d still have access until November 8, but that continued access kept my Hulu account linked to Verizon’s billing. Because of this, I couldn’t sign up for Hulu Live until Verizon released the account on the 8th.Between November 1 and 5, I spent over eight hours in chats and phone calls repeating the same issue. I was told to call Hulu, then told only Verizon could fix it. My case was closed without resolution, and I never received the promised callback.This should have been a simple fix, yet it turned into days of frustration. I’ve always paid on time and stayed loyal, but this experience made me feel my time and loyalty mean nothing to Verizon. I truly hope Verizon takes accountability and improves how it supports long-time customers.

reviews.title: Title: Horrible Service and Unfair Billing Practices
reviews.content: I’ve been a Verizon customer for over 5 years and I’ve never experienced such terrible service. I have a business account, and after I moved to a new location about six months ago, I didn’t even use my Verizon internet once — simply because I hadn’t set up service at my new address yet.About five months ago, I called Verizon to close my account, but their representative convinced me to keep paying for my phone line, saying it would be easier since my equipment was already paid off. I trusted them. That was a huge mistake.Now, after six months of paying for a service I never used, I decided to finally close everything. But when I called, instead of helping me, Verizon forced me to pay for another month — even though I clearly explained that I haven’t been using the service at all.Their customer service is unbelievably slow and unhelpful, their website and mobile app constantly malfunction, and their billing practices are beyond unfair. Verizon only cares about money, not their customers. I’m done with them, and I’ll make sure everyone I know hears about this experience.Stay far away from Verizon — especially if you value honesty and fair treatment

reviews.title: I'll bet Verizon's million-dollar…
reviews.content: I'll bet Verizon's million-dollar executives are scratching their heads over their Champagne-and-caviar lunches, wondering why T-Mobile is eating their lunch and stealing their customers. I'll also bet that is why they have had to lease data space to Cox Communications for their new Cox Mobile service at significant savings over their own pricing. This kind of business strategy is thoughtless at best, and suicidal at worst. Cox's entry and use of Verizon's towers will only hasten Verizon's demise as the premier carrier in the United States. In fact, Cox goes so far as to stop "just short" of advertising that it uses Verizon towers. And when you talk with Cox Mobile salespeople, all they speak about is that they're running on Verizon's network. I wonder, and scratch my head, walking into the local corporate Verizon store and see two, maybe three customers milling about, waiting for four, yes, four, Verizon salespeople who are laughing and talking amongst themselves, why Verizon now finds itself in the position it is in.I waited over ten minutes last night at the Verizon store after leaving the T-Mobile store across the street. T-Mobile had five or six working staffers trying to keep up with twice as many customers. And Verizon continues to wonder — and is only now trying to catch up — with all sorts of incentives for new and existing customers. And by the way, those "incentives" come with all kinds of contractual agreements, including three years of indentured servitude to Verizon.While T-Mobile has its share of problems — it has oversold its services, has inadequately trained Filipino agents, and hour-plus-long phone and in-store wait times — Cox Mobile also has significant issues, having tried to enter the realm of Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T on two prior occasions and failed abysmally each time. And Cox also has incompetent offshore contracted agents, just as T-Mobile, Verizon, and AT&T do. And let's not forget AT&T, with ridiculously high prices, poor offshore customer service, and faltering service. Does anyone wonder whether Verizon will be the ultimate loser in this scenario, just as Sears, Pan Am, Kmart, and TWA, and a host of others, who thought they were too large and important to fail?If I were Verizon, I'd start brown-bagging it instead of caviar and Champagne, and look within, instead of what they've been doing for years. The market is changing, and Verizon needs to adapt. It's time to compete with intelligence, not just size and reputation.

reviews.content: We’ve been with Verizon for 30+ years! And now we’ve been lied to enough!!! Spoke with a representative early August, was told we were eligible for new phones at no cost, (we had to send old phones in) no problem!! LIES LIES apparently! Spent part of the month of August and all of September speaking with various representatives, and receiving various explanations!!! Seems each had their own agenda!!  Got frustrated and emailed Excutive services. Thought that maybe someone might actually do their job! WRONG! I gave her dates, times, and names of individuals that I had spoken with! She assured me she would get the answers! LIES!!!! She called me a month later and says that the charges are accurate?? I asked her if she had listened to the call from August 2nd in reference to the phones being free? She replied that she had NOT! I asked her to review the conversation with myself on the phone! I asked her to do that, she stated that she could not listen to the call because it was now too late as they only keep the recording for 30 days?? Now Verizon wants to charge me exonerated fees and equipment charges! I try to remain loyal as I’m a small business owner myself. Guess it’s time to move to a new carrier (T-Mobile is eager for my business)

reviews.title: What a nightmare and I’ve only been a…
reviews.content: What a nightmare and I’ve only been a business customer for 2 days! I should have known this wasn’t going to go well when I realized my Account Rep, who is trying to sign me up and sell me services for my business, didn’t have a direct phone or email address and could only call me after initiate a request. Keep in mind this is the most important and involved interaction I’ll probably ever have with Verizon and the time they should be most eager to talk to me but no, even now I am kept at arms length and denied the ability to call my sales rep to work on my corporate transfer. I can just imagine what trying to speak to someone will be like when the contracts are all signed. On top of this, the transfer has been a total fail. So many problems, devices that are unusable due to problems with porting, compatibility and shipping. Total frustration but I can’t speak to anyone. No less than a dozen times I’ve tried to call for help only to get trapped in their Orwellian phone directly and an answering AI who lives to simply hang up on you when you can’t answer a question you couldn’t possibly know. The best you can hope for is being directed to a another customer service number which will waste just as much of your time. You cannot bypass the system. You cannot beg the AI for human assistance or push any button to direct to live help. Even the website chat windows takes a science degree to navigate to place that will allow a human to assist you. Once you get in the queue they hit you with the “volume is high” excuse like they’ve never answered a chat before and you are forced to wait 30+ minutes for help. Good look once you get it because verifying yourself will make you wish you’d just accepted your fate and choose to string two cans together instead. Hate this company and their complete lack of service.

reviews.title: Loyal Customer Ignored After 8 Hours of Calls and No Resolution
reviews.content: I’veI’ve been a loyal Verizon customer for many years, but this recent experience left me feeling completely unvalued. On November 1, 2025, I canceled my Disney, Hulu, and ESPN bundle through the Verizon app because I wanted to open a Hulu + Live TV account. Verizon doesn’t allow that upgrade within the bundle, so I removed it. The app said I’d still have access until November 8, but that continued access kept my Hulu account linked to Verizon’s billing. Because of this, I couldn’t sign up for Hulu Live until Verizon released the account on the 8th.Between November 1 and 5, I spent over eight hours in chats and phone calls repeating the same issue. I was told to call Hulu, then told only Verizon could fix it. My case was closed without resolution, and I never received the promised callback.This should have been a simple fix, yet it turned into days of frustration. I’ve always paid on time and stayed loyal, but this experience made me feel my time and loyalty mean nothing to Verizon. I truly hope Verizon takes accountability and improves how it supports long-time customers.

reviews.title: Title: Horrible Service and Unfair Billing Practices
reviews.content: I’ve been a Verizon customer for over 5 years and I’ve never experienced such terrible service. I have a business account, and after I moved to a new location about six months ago, I didn’t even use my Verizon internet once — simply because I hadn’t set up service at my new address yet.About five months ago, I called Verizon to close my account, but their representative convinced me to keep paying for my phone line, saying it would be easier since my equipment was already paid off. I trusted them. That was a huge mistake.Now, after six months of paying for a service I never used, I decided to finally close everything. But when I called, instead of helping me, Verizon forced me to pay for another month — even though I clearly explained that I haven’t been using the service at all.Their customer service is unbelievably slow and unhelpful, their website and mobile app constantly malfunction, and their billing practices are beyond unfair. Verizon only cares about money, not their customers. I’m done with them, and I’ll make sure everyone I know hears about this experience.Stay far away from Verizon — especially if you value honesty and fair treatment

reviews.title: I'll bet Verizon's million-dollar…
reviews.content: I'll bet Verizon's million-dollar executives are scratching their heads over their Champagne-and-caviar lunches, wondering why T-Mobile is eating their lunch and stealing their customers. I'll also bet that is why they have had to lease data space to Cox Communications for their new Cox Mobile service at significant savings over their own pricing. This kind of business strategy is thoughtless at best, and suicidal at worst. Cox's entry and use of Verizon's towers will only hasten Verizon's demise as the premier carrier in the United States. In fact, Cox goes so far as to stop "just short" of advertising that it uses Verizon towers. And when you talk with Cox Mobile salespeople, all they speak about is that they're running on Verizon's network. I wonder, and scratch my head, walking into the local corporate Verizon store and see two, maybe three customers milling about, waiting for four, yes, four, Verizon salespeople who are laughing and talking amongst themselves, why Verizon now finds itself in the position it is in.I waited over ten minutes last night at the Verizon store after leaving the T-Mobile store across the street. T-Mobile had five or six working staffers trying to keep up with twice as many customers. And Verizon continues to wonder — and is only now trying to catch up — with all sorts of incentives for new and existing customers. And by the way, those "incentives" come with all kinds of contractual agreements, including three years of indentured servitude to Verizon.While T-Mobile has its share of problems — it has oversold its services, has inadequately trained Filipino agents, and hour-plus-long phone and in-store wait times — Cox Mobile also has significant issues, having tried to enter the realm of Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T on two prior occasions and failed abysmally each time. And Cox also has incompetent offshore contracted agents, just as T-Mobile, Verizon, and AT&T do. And let's not forget AT&T, with ridiculously high prices, poor offshore customer service, and faltering service. Does anyone wonder whether Verizon will be the ultimate loser in this scenario, just as Sears, Pan Am, Kmart, and TWA, and a host of others, who thought they were too large and important to fail?If I were Verizon, I'd start brown-bagging it instead of caviar and Champagne, and look within, instead of what they've been doing for years. The market is changing, and Verizon needs to adapt. It's time to compete with intelligence, not just size and reputation.

reviews.title: I started service with Verizon from…
reviews.content: I started service with Verizon from August 2, 2025, and disconnected on September 8, 2025. Here's what happened:I was charged twice on my first bill. The first charge was labeled as "First Billing," and the second charge covered the period from August 3 to September 2, 2025 — even though this was all within my first month of service.After I disconnected my line on September 8, Verizon kept my account open until October 4, 2025, and charged me for that extra time without my consent. When I contacted customer service, they blamed it on "company policy" and refused to issue a refund.In summary: I used Verizon's service for 1 month and 6 days, but I was charged for 2 months and 6 days.DON'T DO BUSINESS WITH VERIZON! BIG SCAMMER!

reviews.title: We’ve been with Verizon for 30+ years
reviews.content: We’ve been with Verizon for 30+ years! And now we’ve been lied to enough!!! Spoke with a representative early August, was told we were eligible for new phones at no cost, (we had to send old phones in) no problem!! LIES LIES apparently! Spent part of the month of August and all of September speaking with various representatives, and receiving various explanations!!! Seems each had their own agenda!!  Got frustrated and emailed Excutive services. Thought that maybe someone might actually do their job! WRONG! I gave her dates, times, and names of individuals that I had spoken with! She assured me she would get the answers! LIES!!!! She called me a month later and says that the charges are accurate?? I asked her if she had listened to the call from August 2nd in reference to the phones being free? She replied that she had NOT! I asked her to review the conversation with myself on the phone! She informed me that that wasn’t possible! I asked her if she had listened to the call, she stated that no she had NOT. I asked her to do that, she stated that she could not listen to the call because it was now too late as they only keep the recording for 30 days?? Now Verizon wants to charge me exonerated fees and equipment charges! I try to remain loyal as I’m a small business owner myself. Guess it’s time to move to a new carrier (T-Mobile is eager for my business)

Hate this company and their complete lack of service.

reviews.title: Loyal Customer Ignored After 8 Hours of Calls and No Resolution
reviews.content: I’veI’ve been a loyal Verizon customer for many years, but this recent experience left me feeling completely unvalued. On November 1, 2025, I canceled my Disney, Hulu, and ESPN bundle through the Verizon app because I wanted to open a Hulu + Live TV account. Verizon doesn’t allow that upgrade within the bundle, so I removed it. The app said I’d still have access until November 8, but that continued access kept my Hulu account linked to Verizon’s billing. Because of this, I couldn’t sign up for Hulu Live until Verizon released the account on the 8th.Between November 1 and 5, I spent over eight hours in chats and phone calls repeating the same issue. I was told to call Hulu, then told only Verizon could fix it. My case was closed without resolution, and I never received the promised callback.This should have been a simple fix, yet it turned into days of frustration. I’ve always paid on time and stayed loyal, but this experience made me feel my time and loyalty mean nothing to Verizon. I truly hope Verizon takes accountability and improves how it supports long-time customers.

reviews.title: I'll bet Verizon's million-dollar…
reviews.content: I'll bet Verizon's million-dollar executives are scratching their heads over their Champagne-and-caviar lunches, wondering why T-Mobile is eating their lunch and stealing their customers. I'll also bet that is why they have had to lease data space to Cox Communications for their new Cox Mobile service at significant savings over their own pricing. This kind of business strategy is thoughtless at best, and suicidal at worst. Cox's entry and use of Verizon's towers will only hasten Verizon's demise as the premier carrier in the United States. In fact, Cox goes so far as to stop "just short" of advertising that it uses Verizon towers. And when you talk with Cox Mobile salespeople, all they speak about is that they're running on Verizon's network. I wonder, and scratch my head, walking into the local corporate Verizon store and see two, maybe three customers milling about, waiting for four, yes, four, Verizon salespeople who are laughing and talking amongst themselves, why Verizon now finds itself in the position it is in.I waited over ten minutes last night at the Verizon store after leaving the T-Mobile store across the street. T-Mobile had five or six working staffers trying to keep up with twice as many customers. And Verizon continues to wonder — and is only now trying to catch up — with all sorts of incentives for new and existing customers. And by the way, those "incentives" come with all kinds of contractual agreements, including three years of indentured servitude to Verizon.While T-Mobile has its share of problems — it has oversold its services, has inadequately trained Filipino agents, and hour-plus-long phone and in-store wait times — Cox Mobile also has significant issues, having tried to enter the realm of Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T on two prior occasions and failed abysmally each time. And Cox also has incompetent offshore contracted agents, just as T-Mobile, Verizon, and AT&T do. And let's not forget AT&T, with ridiculously high prices, poor offshore customer service, and faltering service. Does anyone wonder whether Verizon will be the ultimate loser in this scenario, just as Sears, Pan Am, Kmart, and TWA, and a host of others, who thought they were too large and important to fail?If I were Verizon, I'd start brown-bagging it instead of caviar and Champagne, and look within, instead of what they've been doing for years. The market is changing, and Verizon needs to adapt. It's time to compete with intelligence, not just size and reputation.

reviews.title: What a nightmare and I’ve only been a…
reviews.content: What a nightmare and I’ve only been a business customer for 2 days! I should have known this wasn’t going to go well when I realized my Account Rep, who is trying to sign me up and sell me services for my business, didn’t have a direct phone or email address and could only call me after initiate a request. Keep in mind this is the most important and involved interaction I’ll probably ever have with Verizon and the time they should be most eager to talk to me but no, even now I am kept at arms length and denied the ability to call my sales rep to work on my corporate transfer. I can just imagine what trying to speak to someone will be like when the contracts are all signed. On top of this, the transfer has been a total fail. So many problems, devices that are unusable due to problems with porting, compatibility and shipping. Total frustration but I can’t speak to anyone. No less than a dozen times I’ve tried to call for help only to get trapped in their Orwellian phone directly and an answering AI who lives to simply hang up on you when you can’t answer a question you couldn’t possibly know. The best you can hope for is being directed to a another customer service number which will waste just as much of your time. You cannot bypass the system. You cannot beg the AI for human assistance or push any button to direct to live help. Even the website chat windows takes a science degree to navigate to place that will allow a human to assist you. Once you get in the queue they hit you with the “volume is high” excuse like they’ve never answered a chat before and you are forced to wait 30+ minutes for help. Good look once you get it because verifying yourself will make you wish you’d just accepted your fate and choose to string two cans together instead. Hate this company and their complete lack of service.

reviews.title: Loyal Customer Ignored After 8 Hours of Calls and No Resolution
reviews.content: I’veI’ve been a loyal Verizon customer for many years, but this recent experience left me feeling completely unvalued. On November 1, 2025, I canceled my Disney, Hulu, and ESPN bundle through the Verizon app because I wanted to open a Hulu + Live TV account. Verizon doesn’t allow that upgrade within the bundle, so I removed it. The app said I’d still have access until November 8, but that continued access kept my Hulu account linked to Verizon’s billing. Because of this, I couldn’t sign up for Hulu Live until Verizon released the account on the 8th.Between November 1 and 5, I spent over eight hours in chats and phone calls repeating the same issue. I was told to call Hulu, then told only Verizon could fix it. My case was closed without resolution, and I never received the promised callback.This should have been a simple fix, yet it turned into days of frustration. I’ve always paid on time and stayed loyal, but this experience made me feel my time and loyalty mean nothing to Verizon. I truly hope Verizon takes accountability and improves how it supports long-time customers.

reviews.title: Title: Horrible Service and Unfair Billing Practices
reviews.content: I’ve been a Verizon customer for over 5 years and I’ve never experienced such terrible service. I have a business account, and after I moved to a new location about six months ago, I didn’t even use my Verizon internet once — simply because I hadn’t set up service at my new address yet.About five months ago, I called Verizon to close my account, but their representative convinced me to keep paying for my phone line, saying it would be easier since my equipment was already paid off. Verizon only cares about money, not their customers. I’m done with them, and I’ll make sure everyone I know hears about this experience.Stay far away from Verizon — especially if you value honesty and fair treatment

reviews.title: I'll bet Verizon's million-dollar…
reviews.content: I'll bet Verizon's million-dollar executives are scratching their heads over their Champagne-and-caviar lunches, wondering why T-Mobile is eating their lunch and stealing their customers. I'll also bet that is why they have had to lease data space to Cox Communications for their new Cox Mobile service at significant savings over their own pricing. This kind of business strategy is thoughtless at best, and suicidal at worst. Cox's entry and use of Verizon's towers will only hasten Verizon's demise as the premier carrier in the United States. In fact, Cox goes so far as to stop "just short" of advertising that it uses Verizon towers. And when you talk with Cox Mobile salespeople, all they speak about is that they're running on Verizon's network. I wonder, and scratch my head, walking into the local corporate Verizon store and see two, maybe three customers milling about, waiting for four, yes, four, Verizon salespeople who are laughing and talking amongst themselves, why Verizon now finds itself in the position it is in.I waited over ten minutes last night at the Verizon store after leaving the T-Mobile store across the street. T-Mobile had five or six working staffers trying to keep up with twice as many customers. And Verizon continues to wonder — and is only now trying to catch up — with all sorts of incentives for new and existing customers. And by the way, those "incentives" come with all kinds of contractual agreements, including three years of indentured servitude to Verizon.While T-Mobile has its share of problems — it has oversold its services, has inadequately trained Filipino agents, and hour-plus-long phone and in-store wait times — Cox Mobile also has significant issues, having tried to enter the realm of Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T on two prior occasions and failed abysmally each time. And Cox also has incompetent offshore contracted agents, just as T-Mobile, Verizon, and AT&T do. And let's not forget AT&T, with ridiculously high prices, poor offshore customer service, and faltering service. Does anyone wonder whether Verizon will be the ultimate loser in this scenario, just as Sears, Pan Am, Kmart, and TWA, and a host of others, who thought they were too large and important to fail?If I were Verizon, I'd start brown-bagging it instead of caviar and Champagne, and look within, instead of what they've been doing for years. The market is changing, and Verizon needs to adapt. It's time to compete with intelligence, not just size and reputation.

reviews.title: Verizon: Profiting from Misleading Low-Income Consumers and Damaging Credit
reviews.content: In December 2022, a Verizon representative came to my boarding house and informed me that I qualified for free internet service under the Affordable Care Act program. I was assured that my bill would be brought to zero after enrollment.Despite this assurance, I immediately began receiving bills from Verizon. I raised this issue with the original representative, who stated she was having trouble resolving the billing problem and was working with her supervisor. Shortly after, she stopped returning my calls.When Verizon installed the equipment, I already had an outstanding bill, even though I had been promised the charges would be waived. Because the issue remained unresolved, I removed the equipment the next day and returned it to Verizon.From December 2022 through 2023/2024, I made countless phone calls to Verizon customer service. Each time, I was told that the bill was an error and would be removed. Despite these assurances, the balance was never cleared.Verizon eventually referred the account to a collections agency, damaging my credit. I was then told to call/physical mail TSI a company in Pennsylvania (I reside in New Jersey) that was supposedly handling the matter. That company also assured me that the account would be corrected, but nothing changed.In 2025, I received a settlement offer by mail regarding the disputed account. Wanting to clear my credit report, I accepted the offer and paid approximately 50% of the balance. Verizon then reported the account as “paid in full for less than the full balance”, which still appears as a derogatory mark on my credit report.This was misleading. I entered into the settlement with the understanding it would be reflected as “paid in full” without derogatory language.In August 2025, I filed a complaint with the FCC. Verizon contacted me following that complaint. I explained the entire situation again. After an internal review, Verizon told me the reason the bill was not set to zero was that I had been “emailed and told to set up the account myself.” However, this is not what I was told by the original Verizon representative. She stated explicitly that she would handle the setup.At every stage, Verizon representatives acknowledged the billing issue and repeatedly assured me it would be resolved. Despite my returning the equipment promptly and making multiple attempts to resolve the matter, Verizon has refused to correct the derogatory reporting.Result:My credit report continues to show a derogatory remark from Verizon that should not exist. I was misled into believing the account would be resolved and later misled into paying a settlement that did not remove the negative reporting. This has caused ongoing harm to my credit.So after years of repeated calls, promises, and a settlement payment to clear my credit, Verizon has refused to remove the derogatory mark — a small correction that would cost them nothing but continues to harm me. It is unscrupulous that such an exceedingly wealthy company profits from misleading low-income consumers and refuses to correct errors, even after taking money for a service I never used.

reviews.title: Verizon's Broken System Cost Me Time, Service, and Frustration — With No Resolution
reviews.content: I’ve been a Verizon customer for 7 years, with 9 phone lines and home internet. On August 10, 2025, I completed a phone order for a new line and two line upgrades. I received the new line, but never got the upgrade devices.After waiting nearly 2 hours on a customer service call, I was told the order was stuck waiting for supervisor approval and to call back in 3 business days. When I followed up 11 days later, I was told the order had been canceled without any explanation.Escalating to a supervisor, I was told that Verizon’s system failed to process the order and the agent never sent me confirmation. Despite acknowledging the error, Verizon did not offer any kind of compensation — just an apology.For a loyal customer managing multiple lines, this was a frustrating and disappointing experience. Verizon needs to take more responsibility when its systems and agents fail.

Verizon has no respect for veterans, police, or families in crisis. It’s sickening.

reviews.title: Formal Complaint Against Verizon Wireless – Failure to Fulfill Order, Inaccessible Customer Support, and Repeated Service FailuresFormal Complaint Against Verizon…
reviews.content: Formal Complaint Against Verizon Wireless – Failure to Fulfill Order, Inaccessible Customer Support, and Repeated Service Failures To Whom It May Concern,I am submitting this complaint regarding Verizon Wireless due to a persistent and unresolved issue related to an order I placed for a prepaid mobile hotspot (Jetpack device), along with serious failures in customer service and support accessibility.On July 17th, 2025, I placed a phone order with Verizon for a Jetpack device and prepaid service. I confirmed my full shipping address multiple times during the call with their representative. However, I later received an email indicating that the address was incomplete. As a result, the order was flagged and appears to have never been properly shipped—despite my immediate and repeated efforts to resolve the issue.Here is a detailed outline of the obstacles I have faced in attempting to resolve this matter:1. Incomplete Order FulfillmentDespite verbal confirmation of my full address with the Verizon agent, I received a notice indicating only a partial address was recorded.The tracking portal shows no delivery or correction, and the order status has not updated meaningfully since.2. Repeated Disconnections and Broken Promises from SupportI called Verizon support at least 4–5 times, only to be disconnected mid-call.On my most recent call, a representative acknowledged the issue, assured me it would be corrected with the help of a supervisor, and promised a callback if disconnected. That callback never came.On subsequent attempts, I was immediately routed out of the system after ID verification, with an automated voice saying, “Thank you for calling Verizon, goodbye.”3. Online Chat and Account Access BarriersI attempted to resolve the issue via online chat, but was prompted to create an account, which I did.After entering all required information (email, password, ZIP, etc.), I was told my data “did not match our records.”Despite providing my order number and lockdown reference number, I could not reach a human agent or progress any further through chat.4. Total Lack of Accountability or ContactVerizon has provided no accessible way to speak with a representative, no follow-up, and no resolution to date.I have exhausted every communication method offered and am now completely locked out of the support system despite already paying for the product and service.Consumer Impact:This level of inaccessibility and lack of accountability is unacceptable—especially for a utility-grade service essential for secure online access in rural areas. I rely on mobile internet for basic banking, telehealth, online payments, and communication. Verizon’s failures have left me without service, out-of-pocket for a product I have not received, and with no support recourse.I am requesting that Verizon Wireless be required to:1. Correct the shipping error and complete delivery of my paid order.2. Improve transparency and access to customer support services.3. Issue a refund or provide timely fulfillment if resolution is not possible.Order Information:Order Number: XXXXXXLockdown/Location Code: XXXXXCorrect Shipping Address:XXXXXXContact Phone: XXXXXPlease confirm receipt of this complaint and let me know how it will be processed. I am available for additional documentation or verification as needed.Sincerely,BC

reviews.title: Avoid Verizon at all cost
reviews.content: Verizon sent a $106.44 WITH INTEREST charge to collections from an old account I could no longer access. Originally, I had Account A, but after upgrading my Fios service, Verizon closed that account and created a new one (Account B). From that point on, whenever I logged in, I was only shown Account B—my new, active account—with a $0 balance. The old account was essentially hidden. I received no clear notice that Account A had a balance, nor any way to view or manage it through my login.I contacted Verizon support multiple times before the collections hit, and each time they told me my account was in good standing. Not one representative ever mentioned the existence of Account A, even when I directly asked if there could be any other accounts tied to me. I only found out after a collection item appeared on my credit report. I then contacted the collections agency and learned the $106.44 charge came from the old, hidden account. I paid it in full to avoid hurting credit score.After that, I filed a complaint with the Better Business Bureau (BBB). A Verizon rep reached out, but did absolutely nothing. I emailed to explain that the credit bureau had investigated and told me Verizon confirmed the debt, but didn’t address any of my concerns about system failure or lack of access. The rep didn’t respond to my email—just called days later to say, “If that’s what the credit bureau said, then that’s it,” and asked to close the BBB case. No accountability, no explanation, no help.Verizon keeps repeating that their records show the charge was valid—but that’s not the point. The issue is that I couldn’t see or pay that charge because Verizon erased my access when they opened the new account. Their system gave me no visibility into Account A, and their support gave me no answers when I tried to ask.This isn’t just a billing issue—it’s a customer service and systems failure. Verizon's inaction, misleading account management, and refusal to take responsibility caused real damage to my credit for a charge I had no fair chance to resolve

reviews.title: Don't Even Try the 30-Day Free Trail
reviews.content: On July 3, 2025, I walked into a Verizon corporate store and spoke with a (very nice) young man about trying the Verizon 30-day free trial.  The young salesman was able to determine that the trail was ONLY available online.Today (July 4th), I followed the steps online to setup my 30-day free trial on my iPhone 16 Pro Max (unlocked with an available eSIM).  I received an email indicating my temporary cell number at 9:33am CST.After four hours I still had no Verizon trial service.  After calling customer support at 1:24pm CST, being transferred to four different individuals -- the last of which was "inside sales" and the completely wrong person to speak with -- I spoke with the fifth person who had such a strong accent AND garbled audio that they disconnected my call... after trying to get help for 47 minutes.I call back, eventually get transferred to a "supervisor".  The call, while active, was "dead air" -- NO ONE WAS ON THE LINE.If Verizon cannot even handle something as utterly simple as a 30-day trial period for a prospective customer, I sincerely feel bad for anyone needing Verizon for actual business or personal use.T-Mobile 5G cellular internet sucks, but at least they respond to calls properly.  Looks like it's time to try AT&T.UPDATE:  Several more tech support individuals confirmed that because I don't have an actual Verizon account -- it's only a free trial -- there is nothing they can do to troubleshoot this issue.  And, because I've already used the Verizon app to try access to the free trial, I cannot re-signup for the free trial.  This is literally a "bait-and-switch" operation being run by Verizon.

reviews.title: Stay far,far away from Verizon business…
reviews.content: Stay far,far away from Verizon business and Verizon wireless.We signed our business up for service with Verizon Business and it's been pure hell since.The day we signed up I had to contact them to verify our business address, license and fed tax ID, along with my own personal identity. I completed all of the requested verifications and document uploads.I then got in contact with a business rep to help me complete the process as it was being weird and kept hanging/freezing.The rep had me do ALL of the verifications again, then finally approved my account, opened it and submitted my order for me. I got an email with a PIN number that I had to plug-in on their site to add my payment info and complete the order.Finally, hours later I thought I was home free. I inout my payment info, submitted the order, the screen thanked me and verified I completed everything. Then, a notification popped up on my phone to let me know my payment to Verizon was successful and my bank was charged.Hours go by and I never receive a confirmation email not does my order show up in my business account.I contact Verizon again, worried something is wrong. They inform me I have to now contact the fraud department to verify my info ... FOR THE THIRD TIME.This time the rep is nice at first, then suddenly is a complete smart ass and tells me I need to submit MORE DOCUMENTATION. Before I can even ask any questions she is rushing me off the phone trying to hang up with zero explanation.So they can charge my bank account with zero issues ... allow an employee to personally verify my account and create the order for me but then turn around and claim they need even more bullshit to verify our business and cancel the order.What in the hell is wrong with this place? How many damn times do they need to verify someone before they are satisfied? How many times does one employee verify someone but the next doesn't? Why do they think it's ok to take my damn money and then not deliver the goods/services I paid for?Im trying to run a a damn business here. I don't have time to babysit their employees or verify my identity 78 times.Is this a common theme with them? Im trying to decide if I should continue trying to get my damn phone or if I should just go somewhere else.

reviews.title: Unreliable Protection Plan & Poor Customer Support
reviews.content: My wife had to replace her phone through Verizon’s protection plan with Asurion. The first replacement phone only lasted two to three days, so we had to request a second replacement.During this process, Verizon sold my wife a Home Protection Plan, making it sound like something she needed for the phone — which it wasn't. When we realized the mistake and called to cancel that plan, Verizon mistakenly canceled both the Home Protection Plan and the actual phone protection plan — without notifying us.Now the second replacement phone has failed (still within its one-year warranty), but Asurion refuses to honor the protection plan because Verizon had dropped the policy. When we contacted Verizon for help, they couldn’t provide details about who handled the call or offer any notes on what was said. Because of their mistake, we’re unable to get the phone replaced.The only thing Verizon offered was a standard trade-in deal, which still requires us to pay out of pocket — essentially the same deal anyone would get without having had insurance. It completely defeats the purpose of having paid for a protection plan in the first place.In the end, we paid over $300 into Verizon and Asurion’s protection plans and now have to spend $650 for a new phone — putting us out almost $1,000. Had we skipped the plan and saved the money ourselves, we’d be much better off. We would have had to only put up half the price of a new phone.  It’s clear that Verizon is more interested in maximizing profits than taking responsibility for their mistakes.Verizon's mistake was very costly on us.

reviews.title: Frustrating Experience with Verizon’s Fraud Department and Customer Service
reviews.content: I came to Verizon ready to spend over $600 upfront and nearly $200/month on a new phone, iPad, and smartwatch—but what followed was one of the most frustrating customer service experiences I’ve had.My account was quietly placed on hold by the fraud prevention department without any clear communication. Instead of a notification or explanation, I was met with vague error messages on the website when trying to track my order.Over the course of three days, I called multiple times, provided all my identity documents—including a scanned copy of my Social Security Number—and followed every step I was told. Each rep gave me different and often conflicting guidance. In the end, I was told that even submitting all of that still wasn’t sufficient to lift the hold.This lack of transparency, accountability, and coordination is unacceptable—especially when I came fully prepared and eager to become a loyal customer. Verizon needs to do better.

On March 7th, Verizon took $437.94 from my bank account without an invoice or description of what the money was for or my permission.  I then had to cancel my bank debit card after consulting with my lawyer.  I paid off the phones in full with the money I received from T Mobile.  Now, Verizon is claiming that I did not return the internet equipment and saying I am negligent with paying them an addition $493.  I have tried to contact them several times and they refuse to help me but instead harass me with phone calls from a 'Food Lion' phone number.  I am requesting a refund for the $437.94 and help with them to stop harrassing me and acting like I owe them additional money.  I am a single mom who is a teacher and this is causing me a lot of stress.

reviews.title: 11 years with Verizon. No upgrades. Loyalty means nothing.
reviews.content: I’ve been a Verizon Wireless customer for over 11 years with five active lines. I’ve never missed a single payment and have paid over $255/month for years.In all that time, I’ve never received a single upgrade or loyalty offer—nothing to reward my long-term commitment. Meanwhile, new customers are getting premium phones and steep discounts just for switching.I recently reached out via chat to ask for a more competitive plan and upgraded devices—something in line with what they offer to new subscribers. I was told flat-out that they couldn’t help and refused to escalate me to anyone from retention or customer loyalty.Verizon has made it clear they only value new customers. After more than a decade, I’m now preparing to leave. They’ve had every opportunity to make this right.

reviews.title: Horrible business practices
reviews.content: Just when I thought Verizon was tired of their horrible reviews and FTC fines and was making an effort to be a less offensive consumer company, they went back to their rotten roots. We made the mistake of upgrading our phones with Verizon. Like others we got hammered. Their phones are "locked phones" meaning you are locked into Verizon. Verizon loaded over 70 apps and changed all of our settings on the new phone set up. They then charged us $30x2 for this abusive service. They said our former phone plan was no longer available and we had to take an "unlimited plan" One time UNDEFINED charges of $65 and $28 on top of the other unfair charges, represents the ultimate rotten tech company practices. It took us two weeks and two trips to the Verizon store to get all of the settings and unwanted apps removed or disabled. Still having to deal with Google "enable play" harassing pop ups every minute. I will give Verizon credit for the changes they made to MyVerizon on line app. Much more information is now available and the common billing complaints are being addressed. Customer Service is a new night mare. No more domestic English speaking help desk people. All calls now go to an overseas no English, no knowledge of plans no service contractor. Horrible.

reviews.title: So long Verizon
reviews.content: I spent 4 weeks trying to upgrade to the new 16 Pro and after numerous phone calls and multiple visits to the location on State Rd 7 in Wellington Florida this is all I can say.This location has some of the most arrogant male staff members I’ve had the displeasure of dealing with since leaving Miami. In fact, I was so fed up with the blatant machismo that when the service member I was working with began blatantly lying to me about the collaboration between Apple and Verizon I finally called him on it. His response was aggressive and I told the late 20-mid 30 year old man that I don’t accept sass from the students I teach and I absolutely wasn’t going to accept it from him either so he’d better curb his attitude. He told me to leave the store and I told him I’d absolutely do that.  After 20 years of loyalty to Verizon I went up the road to T-Mobile where I transferred service for myself, my husband, my mother, and my 2 teens; a total of 11 lines for phones, iPads, and watches. We purchased an Apple 16 Pro Max for each adult and an Apple 14 for the kids. I also persuaded my adult daughter and her husband to switch their service over as well. I don’t teach math or economics but I think that the total loss of revenue might have made it more advantageous for Verizon to get rid of their less congenial employees and work on customer retention instead. I’m a brand loyalist to the core but I unequivocally refuse to reward your lack of customer care and loyalty with my hard earned money.

reviews.title: The Phone Plan(and company) from HELL!
reviews.content: First of all I was completely scammed and ripped off when I signed up with Verizon at a "Verizon Store of the Year" here In Olathe, Kansas as I traded in my Google Pixel 6 Pro for an iPhone 15. I told the head rip con-person there that all I needed was talk and text, no data at all. She told me "no problem, you need the Welcome plan with unlimited talk and text and a small amount of data. They gave me a small trade in for my phone and set up my iPhone for me and I signed on the dotted line and coughed up the cash needed. When I got home I figured I should log in to my account on the Verizon website. When I checked my account, to my dismay I was signed up to the Unlimited plan at over TWICE THE PRICE. I called this store and was told no problem just change your plan on the website. When I tried that I was immediately told that if I changed it I had to cough up the $900 plus I would owe for my phone! I called Verizon and they told me that it WASN'T THEIR STORE! I was responsible for it. The Verizon store of the year thing means NOTHING. I am retired, disabled and live on disability SQUAT! I have to have a phone, I don't even drive because I cant afford to. THAT is just the beginning of my mess with Verizon! Since buying that phone and THAT plan, I have been CONSTANTLY screwed by their lack of customer support(it takes at LEAST an hour to get a rep on the phone) and loss of service/coverage. Their website SUCKS as it is overly complicated and downright dysfunctional. The overhyped app SUCKS even more than the website. It never works! Now, the THIEVES end me a text message telling me pay up or else when I HAVE PAID, so once again I am on the phone. THIS TIME it took over TWO HOURS to get by their IGNORANT Chatbot and Virtual assistant BS before I got a rep that told me that if the app said I was paid up it must be so. By this time I was so mad that I told them I would ignore all such texts and if they cut me off they will PAY HELL before they get this iPhone that I STILL OWE ON back and that they can TRY to take me to court for it! I also told them that they cant get one dime out of me as I am on Social Security which cannot be garnished! The poor rep I talked to told me he would get me a $10 discount on my bill and I told him what he could do with that, so he upped the discount to $20 a month. That goes to show how they OVERCHARGE because if they have that much leeway in their pricing, they GOUGE the average person by at least that much! Well, they jacked with the WRONG SENIOR DISABLEE HERE! I already made one such review on Yelp and boy did that get noticed. Now, I am here and I won't stop here either. People need to know that VERIZON is a HORRIBLE company that RIPS OFF OLD PEOPLE, DISABLED PEOPLE, and POOR PEOPLE and most likely EVERYBODY THEY CAN! I wouldn't wish VERIZON on Adolph Hitler or the DEVIL himself, although I think he sets on their Board of Director's.....Chairman of the Board! Anybody that has to work there must need a job real bad and I pity them. I would go hungry before working for such a LOW LIFE outfit as VERIZON!

reviews.title: Straight Talk - no straight talk from customer service
reviews.content: This is regarding Straight Talk which Walmart and Verizon are the major owners of this company. They should be ashamed of these poor reviews that they are getting.We are a small organization that provides long-term housing to unhoused individuals. There are a handful of tenants who require a landline. A previous employee set them up with Straight Talk landlines. Getting information to pay the bill and to straighten out issues has been a nightmare. There is still one number that I cannot access on-line - even though we pay the bill each month.The recent concern has been with a dead modem. It took awhile to diagnose the concern. When I first called their customer service number I was told that it was within warranty and would be replaced free of charge. I was not told that it would not be replaced until the broken device was return. This happened on Saturday of Memorial Day Weekend. A few days later I happened to check my email and saw that I needed to take the broken device to UPS. Supposedly there was a free shipping label in the email. I could not open it. When I took it to the UPS store on Tuesday they also could not open it - even though it stated that they would be able to. It has now been over a week that our tenant has been without a phone.I called today to inquire about the shipping label. The person apologized and then sent me another one that had the same format as the first. She gave me a number that UPS could call when I got to the store to obtain the label. Well, this number that I called informed me that the modem was no longer under warranty and was not replaceable free of charge. That is why the shipping label was not available. Every other person that I spoke with assured me that it was under warranty. One person even told me that it was packed up and ready for shipping as soon as UPS scanned the defective one in. I wasted precious time traveling to the UPS, contacting customer service and assuring our tenant that it was in the mail.To top it off, I was then told that I could go to Dollar General, Walmart or Target to purchase a new modem. Again, I wasted time by going to 2 Dollar Generals to be told that they don't carry Straight Talk. Walmart did not have the item in stock at the store that I went to. I ordered it on-line for pickup this afternoon at another local store. An hour later I received a text saying that it was unavailable in the store and could be shipped to me in 2 days. Unfortunately I have little recourse but to wait until Friday. This is not ideal for our tenant who has enough on his plate.The lack of correct information is appalling and frustrating. Due to the small tight budget that we live on, we don't have other affordable options. As soon as I find one, I am dropping this service like a hot potato.

reviews.title: False promissess that will cost you big
reviews.content: I’ve been a loyal Verizon customer for years, but my recent experience has left me deeply disappointed. About 10 months ago, enticed by the promise of affordable internet at $29 a month without any contractual obligations or equipment fees, I made the switch from Comcast. However, what seemed like a fantastic deal quickly turned sour as my bill skyrocketed to over $80 a month. Despite numerous calls to customer service and providing the name and contact information of the initial salesman who set up my account, I learned today that none of the representatives made any note of my concerns or contacted him for clarification. This lack of accountability and transparency is unacceptable.After about nine months, I unfortunately had to close my business, rendering the equipment and service from Verizon unnecessary. To my dismay, I discovered that I’m on a payment plan for the device, making it impossible to return. Now, I’m faced with having to pay almost $300 for equipment that serves me no purpose whatsoever, adding to my frustration. This entire ordeal has been extremely costly, and I feel compelled to warn others not to follow my footsteps and risk being cheated by Verizon.

reviews.title: Unreliable service, unauthorized charge, poor customer service
reviews.content: I have lost Internet connectivity twice, for 4-5 days, between November and March. In the November case, Verizon took its time about fixing the DSL problem after telling me it needed a card for the DSL connection station a mile or so from where I live, and could not get one.At the end of February, my DSL went out again. They diagnosed the problem as outside my house, and closed the ticket but without fixing the problem and without even trying to confirm correction. When I called back, they said it was inside my house and a technician visit would cost $99 (as I recall) to fix the wiring but, if the problem was not in my house, there would be no charge. The technician determined there was no problem in my house, and Verizon had messed up. He went to the outside connection station and fixed it very quickly (for which he personally deserves a 5 out of 5 star rating).I just saw my bill to which $159 had been added, i.e. more than Verizon said it would charge, even though I owed nothing because the problem was not with my wiring. I just called Verizon to get this corrected and I assume they will do so, but their call system called me back (when a representative was supposed to be available) and then told me I had to wait because all representatives were busy. This is blatant disrespect for my time.The only reason I don't drop them on the spot and find another service provider is that it would take me a long time to update my E-mail contact information for a lot of web sites and people.This review is based on my experience today and in the past several months, and I have not received any incentives to write it.Update April 4; although their representative (about a week ago) committed to investigating the unauthorized $159 charge for in home service (not owed to them because the problem was outside my house) but my credit card was charged for this anyway. The supervisor to whom I spoke on Apr. 4 refused to do more than refund $60 for phone jack service which had not been needed nor was it performed. I now intend to tell my credit card company to deny payment for the unauthorized charge.Update Apr. 5  Verizon's Executive Team got back to me today in response to a BBB complaint and promised to credit the $159 plus tax to next month's bill. This doesn't change the fact that the things described above happened but, as they have in fact corrected it as soon as they got the BBB complaint, I have changed the rating from one star to two.Update June 2 2024; my phone simply stopped working for no reason. I did the check by connecting a handset to the outside jack and got no dial tone. UPDATE although Verizon told me initially it would not be until June 13 that they could restore my phone service, they did, after some prodding from me, restore it yesterday. The service technician did a great job and the customer support reps also tried to be helpful, and did their best with what they had to work with.UPDATE Oct. 10 2024  Verizon again left me stranded with no Internet and, two days later, no phone service. There was a commitment to fix my phone today but it is now after 5:30 PM and it still does not work. I called support only to have the Verizon "Assistant" ignore keypad entries and say it did not understand me. The phone number for the Verizon Store on Schechter Drive is absolutely worthless as it does not connect with the store.I did install 5G to replace my unreliable DSL service, and it has worked so far. The only reason I didn't switch providers is I would have to get a new E-mail address and switch it for more than 100 web sites and contacts. Service reps try to be helpful, though.

I was charged for 2 temp numbers that are used before porting our numbers. $84.70 was deducted from the next bill. I had to call Verizon and fix their mistake by myself because the clerk wouldn't bother to fix their own mistake.In addition to all these, I had to pay $22.36 for one of the devices for 36 months (totals $737.88), and after 2 months of back and forth, now it's reduced to $5.14 (I guess it's the sales tax, but the other device is only $0.28/mo for some reason).At this point;•	I had to pay unmentioned charges,•	I was charged for temp numbers that I don't own (fixed by myself),•	I had to pay monthly for one of the devices and am still paying a smaller amount (partially fixed to an acceptable amount), and•	I still pay about $30 more for my unlimited plan than what I was told.My sales clerk gave me his private number to help me out, so that I wouldn't keep coming to the store. and I thought that was big help, but these 4 things combined somewhat suggest otherwise. I've been to the Verizon store 7 times and texted the guy for 2 months to fix these errors, I mean how difficult can it be for a Verizon store to fix accounting errors. I was stalled each time I texted, asked to wait. When I first moved to Verizon, he said "the numbers might bounce back and forth for about 2 weeks until the promo code finally sets in". But the numbers never bounced. After that, the answers were very similar every time I texted. "I submitted a ticket, or I did this and that, it should take X days to reflect in your account", X being 1 to 7 days. This went on for 2 months! Then I started receiving answers slower to never. I really find it hard to believe that this cannot be sorted out by a Verizon store. I was either lied to in the beginning or they did not hard enough.I was going to return all the devices and ask for refund, but we decided to forget about it and move on, because it doesn't really hurt my income. But that doesn't mean I'll keep quiet about it.  Trustpilot is next, and then maybe twitter or reddit or whatever if I get time.My recommendation to everyone who's having a similar experience is to simply return everything and get your money back before they stall you until too late. it won't be fixed!

reviews.title: My daughter lost her phone in an…
reviews.content: My daughter lost her phone in an accident last year and when she reported it lost to Verizon they informed her that they couldn’t replace it because it was not insured so they offered a promotion on a new phone with a plan that would remove the service fees on her lost phone so she would only be responsible for the payment of the physical phone. I gave her authorization to manage our phone service at this time.She made payments over the year and got behind a few times so setup up payment arrangements . We had our phones disconnected twice WITHOUT WARNING because the reps did NOT notate it. They’ve added disconnect fees for THIER MISTAKE and refuse to remove/refund.Turns our the promotion was a lie and never attached to our account so we’ve been paying for service and taxes on a phone that remains buried in the desert.Our bills since being late in March 2023, which was paid in April, have ranged from $640-$869 MONTHLY. The past due amount was paid but rolls into each month with “added” charges and NO explanation.Verizon’s $100 million lawsuit specified Deceptive Charges, one in particular being the “Admin & Telco Recovery Charge” of which I specifically asked the Representative “Nick” at corporate in Encinitas, California yesterday and he simply said it’s an admin fee.The only assistance that Nick and his so-called assistant manager offered was to call billing and see what resolution they could off.The connected me with “BILLING” which turned out to be a specialist in SALES who confirmed that the Promotion offered last year did not apply to our account because it wasn’t even being offered (in existence) yet!! Nick said it wasn’t applied because it Expired!! What’s true? Verizon is full of Scheisters they train every employee how to speak in circles.I was on the phone with a representative night before last who kept spinning in circles without ever justifying our exorbitant phone bills no matter how much we paid.BILLING DEPARTMENT (SALES) merely offered a new promotion that would raise our current plan fees! What the fck  right now!!!??!?!?!?

reviews.title: Verizon Incompetence
reviews.content: This review is about Verizon, particularly their Steamtown location in Scranton, Pa. It is the worst Verizon store I have ever had a worse encounter with. The people working there are all incompetent and have no idea what they are doing.September 29th we ordered some cell phone batteries from them. We actually ordered 2 to be is to be exact. This whole fiasco has been a nightmare and believe me it can happen to customers too. Avoid ever ordering anything from this particular Verizon store. You'll never get your parts or items and forget about the big guys at Verizon, they'll just spit in your face.

reviews.title: Verizon Store, Kihei, Maui
reviews.content: Verizon Store, Kihei, Maui, Hawai’iI have had nothing but months and months of trouble after buying a new iPhone 13 at this store. Over 6 months! I purchased a new iPhone 13 pro max here on April 5, 2022. I turned in my iPhone 11 Pro Max as part of the deal. The employee who was helping me said there was only one phone left and because I was in a hurry I didn’t think about it. But the box had been opened. And there was something else wrong. They transferred over everything, but there was a problem with the SIM card. In short, it has been a complete NIGHTMARE. Lost calls, lost texts, and I run my company business off this line. They made some improvements. But it was never quite right.I decided to get a second line, a Maui 808 area code phone number. From that time, the problems increased. It turns out that my original phone number, a 510 area code, was never disconnected from the former iPhone 11. They can’t seem to do that. I have spent well over 8 documented hours on the phone with tech support and it is still not working.It became crucial when recently I was coming back into the country from working in Africa and had severe food poisoning on the plane. When I landed, my daughter could not reach me on either number. I had to go to the ER and we could not connect even after switching the phone on and off. I finally got a text out to her.The phone plan with data roaming cost $252.00 and did not work on either the 510 or 808 lines for most of the time I was away in Southern Africa and Egypt, 6 and 1/2 weeks. My other friends, who were using T-Mobile, had not only great service but it was FREE. Not to mention I heard that you get free Netflix and a year of AARP, if you’re in that age category. No, I don’t work at T-Mobile. But I’m going to get their service for sure.I spent another hour and a half on the phone two days ago, still trying to get the tech department to fix this, and they reassured me it would be handled. Yesterday they called and said “they were working on it”. By 8pm it wasn’t resolved, and I had 2 phone calls come in 6 hours earlier that I never got. The voicemails showed up on my phone, 6 hours late. So then I decided to try again. Last night I spent another hour and a half on the Verizon chat with another agent and after giving the IMEI and ICCID numbers for both lines again, she could not make it work and told me to go get a new SIM card at the Verizon store.WHO IS RESPONSIBLE FOR ALL OF THIS? VERIZON! Apologies for the shouty caps, but really, you people at Verizon, YOU are responsible.And if I am going to get another SIM card, why not get it at T-Mobile? Better service, better prices, better international coverage (free!) and Netflix/AARP.Save your money and buy your phone and your plan in any other store and with any other company than Verizon. Just say NO to Verizon. No.

reviews.title: Don't Fall For Them! You're Gonna Be Stuck Forever! RUN
reviews.content: On April 8, 2022, I contacted customer service to inquire about FIOS internet for my commercial office where I run my small business. In our area of New Jersey, the only options for commercial/business WIFI was either Verizon, or Comcast. Ultimately I chose Verizon due to the fact that Comcast stated I would be required to be in a 2-year contract even though it was $30 cheaper, and I would be penalized if I canceled early within the 2-year contract period. Not wanting to be held down by a 2-year contract I mentioned this concern to the Verizon customer service representative, Marcus Hill, who guaranteed that I would not be locked into a contract and that I could cancel anytime if I did not like the service without penalty.So I moved forward with ordering FIOS. A few months later, I was offered a better deal from another internet provider for much cheaper WIFI so I decided to cancel my Verizon FIOS. I called customer service and the representative, Nicole, unfortunately informed me that I was in fact locked into a 2-year contract, and that I apparently verbally agreed to it when in fact I did not. And if I wanted to cancel my FIOS I would owe a penalty fee of $900.I was never informed about the fact that I was obligated into a contract, or that the promotional pricing I was offered at the time was only offered as contract pricing. If that important information was relayed to me by my original customer service representative, Marcus Hill, then I would've opted for a different company like Comcast who was offering WIFI $30 cheaper at the same 2-year contract term. When I asked customer service representative, Nicole, for proof from her manager of when I verbally agreed to the said 2-year contract, I was flat out denied any form of proof such as a voice recording of the phone call and was told to get a lawyer if I want to get the recording. There is a reason why you have the trash emoji all over social.
